title: Iconic Japanese Artist Yayoi Kusama Dies at 97
paragraphs: Yayoi Kusama, the Japanese artist famous for her polka dots and mirrored rooms, has died at the age of 97. According to her studio, Kusama died at a hospital in Tokyo on August 14, 2026. The studio said that she continued to paint until her final days, never setting aside her brush.

Kusama was born in 1929 in Matsumoto, in Nagano Prefecture. She said that she experienced hallucinations from childhood, and she spent decades in and out of psychiatric institutions. Her parents wanted her to get married, but she chose a different path. In 1957, she moved to New York, becoming one of the first Japanese women to go there to pursue a career in art.

Her early years in New York were difficult, and she lived in poverty for a long time. At that time, a style called "action painting" was popular, but Kusama continued to paint her dots. In the late 1960s, she organized anti-war events called "happenings," in which she put paper dots on people's bodies. These events attracted a lot of media attention. She also became friends with well-known artists such as Andy Warhol and Georgia O'Keeffe.

In addition to painting, Kusama made sculptures, films and installations, and she also wrote novels. Her famous works include "Mirrored Corridor" and "The Visionary Flowers." Later in life, she became extremely successful. She worked with fashion brands like Louis Vuitton, and her designs appeared on products such as teacups and T-shirts. In 2008, one of her works was sold at auction by Christie's for $5.8 million, and in 2016, she received Japan's Order of Culture, the country's top award for artists.
Kusama's work was shown at major museums around the world, including the Museum of Modern Art in New York. In a 2012 interview, she said that she would keep painting until she died.
